## Circular to Management Companies of SFC-authorised Real Estate Investment Trusts ('REITs')

## Acquisitions by SFC-authorised REITs

1. Since the authorisation and listing of the first REIT in November 2005, Hong Kong has seven listed REITs invested in different types of real estate assets both in Hong Kong and in the Mainland. The SFC believes that the Hong Kong REIT market is now ready for  the  next  phase  of  growth.    Experience  in  other  markets  tells  us  that  growth predominantly comes from acquisitions by existing REITs.  The SFC will give its full support to such expansion efforts, whether locally or overseas.
2. In response to some recent feedback from industry participants, the SFC hereby clarifies that in acquiring overseas and/or new types of properties, REIT managers do not have to seek re-approval of their licences or re-authorisation of the relevant REIT by the SFC before  proceeding  to  make  such  acquisitions.    In  other  words,  there  are  no  additional licensing  or  authorisation  requirements  for  REITs  planning  to  expand  their  operations into other markets or jurisdictions or different property types.
3. In making  acquisition decisions, it is the REIT  managers'  obligation  to  satisfy themselves  that  they  have  sufficient  and  appropriate  skills  and  processes  in  place  to manage  the  new  properties,  either  as  part  of  their  in-house  skills  or  by  way  of outsourcing  to  a  competent  external  party  under  their  oversight.    This  would  be  a business decision for REIT  managers  having  regard  to  their  fiduciary  duties to unitholders as a whole.
4. The SFC believes investors expect their REIT managers to manage and grow their REIT businesses.  While a REIT may not have set out any strategic/business plan for growth and  acquisition  in  its  offering  document,  it  may  and  is  entitled  to  develop  new acquisition and growth plans after listing, just like any listed company.  For those new REIT applicants who already have a strategic/business plan for acquisition and growth at the time of listing, they should disclose such plans in their IPO offering documents as investors would like to know about such plans.

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

12 October 2007 Circular to Management Companies of SFC-authorised Real Estate Investment Trusts Acquisitions by SFC-authorised REITs page 2 of 2

5. REIT managers are welcomed to seek further guidance from the SFC on any regulatory aspects concerning their proposed acquisition plans.
6. To enhance regulatory transparency and also as part of our wider initiatives to facilitate the development and growth of the REIT market in Hong Kong, we will issue a separate Circular  to  provide  practical  guidance  on  the  disclosure  and  unitholders'  approval requirements concerning acquisitions by SFC-authorised REITs shortly.
